info.bio:
Bratmobile fue un grupo influenciado principalmente por el indie pop, punk y surf. También fue una de las principales bandas que lideró el movimiento Riot Grrrl!.

En la Universidad de Oregon, Estados Unidos; Allison Wolfe y Molly Newman, colaboraron en una revista llamada "Girl Germs", "los gérmenes de las chicas". La banda tocó su primer concierto en el Club de Surf de el Norte de Olympia (Olympia's North Shore Surf Club), en el día de San Valentín, 1991, siendo tan sólo dos chicas tocando la guitarra, la batería y cantando.

scenes.name: Foxcore y riot grrrls
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El hardcore había sido un fenómeno masculino; el movimiento «riot grrrl» introduce el «factor chica» en la ecuación de frustración, depresión, desesperación y rabia. Nace en Olympia (fanzines como «Girl Germs», el lema «Revolution Girl Style Now!») y bebe de las cantautoras neoyorquinas, las bandas femeninas californianas (Runaways, Frightwig, L7) y las británicas (Raincoats, Slits). Un movimiento fundado en las letras, no en la música: Mecca Normal, Bikini Kill de Kathleen Hanna (y luego Le Tigre), Bratmobile, Team Dresch, Hole de Courtney Love, Seven Year Bitch, Sleater-Kinney. En California, Mudwimin, 4 Non Blondes, Tribe 8, Tiger Trap, Donnas, Red Aunts, That Dog, Muffs; en el Medio Oeste, Babes In Toyland (Fontanelle, «un arte de emociones extremas») y Sugarsmack; Free Kitten y Luscious Jackson en Nueva York.

podcast.title: Early Breakup
podcast.body: By 1994, Bratmobile had broken up. This was part of the general decline of the original Riot Grrrl scene due to various internal and external pressures, including conflicting ideas about media coverage and the co-option of "girl power." "By 1994, Brad Mabel, Evans De Betsy and Huggy Bear had all broken up."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Olympia-based Pioneer
podcast.body: Bratmobile, a three-woman band from Olympia, was an early pioneer in the Riot Grrrl scene. The group emerged from the "widely read feminist zine scene," specifically influenced by a zine called "Girl Germs." "Another early pioneer in this scene we just talked about was Bratmobile. Again they were from Olympia, three women, and again this is a band that grew out of the widely red feminist scene."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Riot Grrrl Band
podcast.body: Bratmobile is mentioned as one of the bands within the Riot Grrrl movement. "And then there were bands like Sugar Baby Doll and the Pagan Babies and Brat Mobio and Heaven's De Betsy and Huggy Bear."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: All-Female Los Angeles Band
xref.body: The Runaways were an all-female band from Los Angeles, famously covered by Bratmobile with their song "Cherry Bomb." They represent an earlier wave of female-fronted rock that influenced later bands like the Riot Grrrl groups. "the all-female band from Los Angeles."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Early Breakup
xref.body: By 1994, Huggy Bear had broken up, mirroring the fate of other original Riot Grrrl bands like Bratmobile and Heavens to Betsy. This breakup was attributed to the intense, political, and emotional nature of the scene, which could not be sustained long-term. "By 1994, Brad Mabel, Evans De Betsy and Huggy Bear had all broken up."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Longevity of Original Riot Grrrl Bands
xref.body: Bikini Kill was the only original Riot Grrrl band to continue performing beyond the mid-90s, lasting until 1997. Most other early bands like Bratmobile, Heavens to Betsy, and Huggy Bear had broken up by 1994 due to internal conflicts and issues surrounding media coverage. "The only original Riot Girl band to make it beyond all that was Bikini Kill. They lasted until 1997."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
